hook: SCP-2191 starts out as a monastery hidden in a Romanian forest and the pale, eyeless things that live inside it. Then the article keeps going down, through older layers of stone and older history, until the scale of the problem changes completely. Expect detailed body horror, including how the creatures feed on paralysed people.
whyItMatters:
This file ties a creature feature to the Sarkic material on the wiki: its interview subject is described as a descendant of the Solomonari, a group a footnote calls a Proto-Sarkic sect, and her account names the Great Karcist and Adytum. It works as an entry point that hints at a much bigger mythology without stopping to explain it.

It is also a strong example of a Foundation ethics file. The closing section is less a containment note than a justification written by people who know exactly what they are permitting.
thingsToNotice:
The structure works like a dig. The temple's Orthodox upper floors are a disguise over Thracian and Dacian levels and tunnels dated to several thousand years BC, and the creatures turn out to be feeding devices: a lamprey-like worm inside each one dissolves victims, other worms carry the nutrients through the walls, and nerve tendrils plug into their spines.

The earthquake timeline is the turn. Disasters across the Balkans from 1932 to 1977 come with sightings of a great serpent, an octopus arm, and pale men taking survivors, revealing SCP-2191-3, an organism whose roots spread across about 660,000 square kilometres. The village elder calls it the Mother, the pregnant concubine of the Great Karcist, and warns it will soon burst. The Foundation's conclusion is that starving it killed roughly 40,000 people, so it now lets the villages keep feeding it sacrifices, and the article ends on the words "Not yet."
